task.title: Move, turn and scale elements
task.shortdesc: A transform moves, turns, scales or skews an element and everything inside it. You choose the functions, the point they turn and scale around, and the box that point is measured in.

info.p: The transform property takes none, the initial value, or a list of functions separated by spaces. These are the functions for a flat drawing:

row.entry: Moves the element. With one value, translate() moves it only to the right or left. Lengths use any unit. A percentage is a part of the width of the reference box for x and of its height for y.
Makes the element larger or smaller. With one value, scale() uses it for both directions. A negative number mirrors the element.
Turns the element clockwise around the transform origin. A positive angle turns clockwise because the y axis goes down.
Slants the element. skewX() moves points sideways in proportion to their height, and skewY() moves them up and down in proportion to their distance from the left. With one value, skew() is skewX().

entry.codeph: matrix(a, b, c, d, e, f)

row.entry: Gives the six numbers of the transform directly. A point x, y goes to a x + c y + e, b x + d y + f.

info.p: Angles use the units deg, grad, rad and turn, and a plain 0 is also an angle. A transform that is not valid is ignored and the element is not transformed.

Each function works in the coordinate system that the functions before it made. In translate(20px, 0) scale(2), the element is scaled first and then moved 20 pixels, so the move is not doubled. In scale(2) translate(20px, 0) the move is also scaled, so it goes 40 pixels.

image.alt: A rectangle with a dashed outline marks the starting place. Six copies of it show a translation, a rotation about the corner, a scaling, a skew, a rotation about the center and a matrix.

info.p: A transform does not change the place of the other elements of the drawing, and it does not change the size that the drawing takes in the text. The elements that follow are drawn as if the transformed element had not moved.
When the transform makes it impossible to go back from the transformed element to the original one, such as scale(0), CSSMedia does not draw the element or its content.

Rotations and scalings happen around a point, the transform origin. In a drawing the origin is the top left corner of the reference box, which is the initial value 0 0. transform-origin moves it. It takes one or two values, and a third length for the third dimension. Each of the first two is a length, a percentage of the reference box, or a keyword: left, center and right for the horizontal position, and top, center and bottom for the vertical one. With one value, the vertical position is the center. When you write a vertical keyword first, as in bottom left, CSSMedia reads it as left bottom.
The percentages of the transform origin, of translate() and of the keywords refer to a reference box. The property transform-box chooses it:

ul.li: view-box, the initial value, is the whole drawing, from its top left corner. With it, transform-origin: 50% 50% is the center of the drawing.
fill-box is the box that holds the shape without its outline. content-box is the same box. For a group, it is the box that holds all the shapes inside it.
stroke-box is the box that also holds the outline. border-box is the same box.

info.p: To turn an element around its own center, use fill-box with transform-origin: center.

A box of your document has no drawing around it, so there view-box, stroke-box and border-box are the border box, and fill-box and content-box are the content box. The initial transform-origin of a box is 50% 50%, its center.

Every function and property of this topic works on the boxes of your document. A box with a transform is drawn on top of the boxes before it, as if it were positioned with z-index: 0, and it is the containing block of the boxes inside it that you position with position: absolute or position: fixed. A transform does not change the place of the other boxes, and it does not apply to inline boxes that hold only text, to table columns or to table column groups. A fixed background-attachment in a transformed box works as scroll. Links inside a transformed box cover the box where it is drawn.

A transform on a table moves the table and its captions as one box, and its reference box is the border box that holds them both. A transform on the root element moves the whole canvas, including the background of the root element, which then fills all that the page shows.
The properties translate, rotate and scale do the work of the functions of the same name, each in a property of its own, so you can change one of them in a rule without repeating the others.

ul.li: translate takes one to three lengths or percentages: x, y and the distance in the third dimension.
rotate takes an angle, which turns the element in the drawing. It can also take an axis, x, y or z or three numbers, and an angle: rotate: x 40deg.
scale takes one to three numbers or percentages. One number scales both directions.

info.p: CSSMedia applies them around the same transform origin as transform, in the order translate, rotate, scale and then the list of transform. The result is the same as writing the functions of the three properties first in one transform.
